data.user_prompt: GEO vs traditional SEO — what changed?

sections.text:
**GEO (Generative Engine Optimization) shifts the focus from ranking high on search results pages to appearing directly in AI-generated answers, fundamentally changing how content visibility works.**[2][3]

## Core Differences

**Traditional SEO** optimized for search engine rankings through keywords, backlinks, and page authority. The goal was to rank high enough that users would click through to your website.[2] **GEO** optimizes for AI credibility and citation—ensuring that language models like ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude recognize your content as trustworthy enough to reference in their synthesized answers.[3]

The shift reflects a change in user behavior: as of 2024, nearly 60% of Google searches in the U.S. end without clicking to any external website, with users instead receiving AI-summarized answers directly.[8]

## What Changed

| Aspect | Traditional SEO | GEO |
|--------|-----------------|-----|
| **Visibility goal** | Rank high on results pages | Appear in AI-generated answers |
| **Keywords** | Exact-match and short-tail terms | Natural, conversational, question-based language |
| **Content strategy** | Keyword-targeted landing pages | High-quality, structured answers to user intent |
| **Trust signals** | Backlinks and domain authority | Author credibility and structured data for AI interpretation |
| **Success metric** | Rankings, click-through rate | Citation frequency, AI visibility |
| **User journey** | Search → click → read | Question → AI answer (with optional click) |

**Context now matters more than exact phrasing.**[6] Instead of optimizing for specific keyword phrases, you optimize for topics and provide comprehensive explanations that AI can extract and cite.[1] Content should use **scannable formats** (headings, bullet points, FAQs) rather than dense paragraphs, making it easier for AI models to pull relevant information.[7]

## What Didn't Change

**GEO does not replace SEO—it builds on it.**[3][4] The foundational practices remain essential: semantic structure, link integrity, content quality, page speed, mobile responsiveness, and technical SEO all still matter.[1][4][5] If your website is poorly structured or lacks authority, GEO optimization alone won't solve those problems.[4]
